welcome: Welcome to your EDC Management Console
addSelectionSubtitle: Choose whether you want to deploy a connector or add an independent component.
edcConnectorOptionHint: Deploy a new Eclipse Dataspace Connector instance.
componentOptionHint: Deploy a submodel service or digital twin registry.
addSelectionTip: Use connectors as the base layer, then attach services and components to them.
connectorNameHelp: Use 3 to 20 lowercase letters, numbers or hyphens, without spaces.
hostnamePlaceholder: Generated automatically from the connector name
hostnameHelp: The hostname is generated automatically from the connector name and the dataspace host suffix.
connectorTypeHelp: Pick the role that best matches how this connector participates in data exchange.
endpointHelp: These endpoints are used to display and manage the connector in the dashboard.
componentsSectionSubtitle: Submodel services, digital twin registries and related services
noConnectorsDescription: Click "Add+" to deploy your first connector.
noComponentsDescription: Add a component as a standalone deployment or link it to one of your connectors.
helpDescription: Find the main onboarding and support entry points for the dashboard.
settingsDescription: These dataspace and platform settings are shown for reference and cannot be modified here.
deleteConnectorMessage: Are you sure you want to delete "{name}"? This action cannot be undone.
deleteComponentMessage: Are you sure you want to delete "{name}"? This action cannot be undone.
dashboardTooltipContent: This is the main workspace where users review status cards, connectors, components and the fastest path to create new items.
dashboardTooltipFooter: Start here when you want the clearest overview of the system.
monitorTooltipContent: This area is intended for operational visibility, health checks and live system tracking.
monitorTooltipFooter: Useful after deployment when you want to verify that integrations remain healthy.
sdeNavContent: Opens the connected SDE application when users want to continue from the console into an exchange workflow.
sdeNavFooter: If this does not open, check the SDE URL in Dataspace Settings first.
portalNavContent: Reserved navigation entry for a portal or broader business-facing application around the dataspace.
portalNavFooter: This can later point to a real portal without changing the navigation pattern.
ichNavContent: Entry point for Industry Core Hub and related platform workflows in the dataspace environment.
ichNavFooter: Useful when teams need access to companion platform applications from one console.
guideReopenContent: Opens the onboarding guide again so users can get step-by-step help whenever they need it.
documentationContent: Opens the application repository with the README, project context and supporting information.
troubleshootingContent: Opens the repository issues page to review known problems and possible fixes.
contactSupportContent: Starts an email support request when the user needs direct help from the responsible team.
settingsTooltipContent: This page shows synchronized dataspace and platform information that often serves as a reference for URLs, environments and system values.
portalPlaceholderDescription: This application entry is ready for a portal integration and can later be connected to a real portal URL or embedded portal experience.
ichPlaceholderDescription: This application entry opens Industry Core Hub and related platform-oriented workflows.
portalRedirectDescription: You will be redirected to the portal application.
sdeRedirectDescription: You will be redirected to the Simple Data Exchanger application.
bpnHelp: Use a valid business partner number in BPNL format.
bpnPrefilledHelp: This BPNL was detected automatically from your login or dataspace information. You can still adjust it if needed.
versionHelp: Stable Tractus-X releases only. The newest version is preselected; pick an older one if you need to match an existing deployment.
versionUnavailableHelp: No deployable version was returned by the dataspace configuration. Contact your dataspace administrator.
deploymentPreparationWelcome: Before you start, choose a valid connector name and review the generated hostname.
deploymentPreparationCredentials: BPNL and technical connector values are loaded automatically from the backend dataspace configuration.
deploymentPreparationExample: Example: for an EDC connector, you will usually need the public API endpoint and the data plane address maintained by your infrastructure or DevOps team.
deploymentEndpointFollowup: If you do not know these URLs yet, ask for the ingress, gateway or service addresses for the control plane and the data plane.
deploymentConnectorOnlyInfo: You are deploying only the EDC connector here. DTR or Submodel Services can be added afterwards as components.
deploymentAutoConfigTitle: BPNL and endpoints are filled automatically.
deploymentAutoConfigDescription: The wizard reads the BPNL and host settings directly from the backend dataspace configuration, so users only need a connector name and the generated hostname.
componentGuidanceChoose: Choose the service type based on its job: Submodel Service for asset data or Digital Twin Registry for registration functions.
componentGuidanceConfig: For the setup you only need a valid component name.
componentGuidanceRestriction: Components and connectors can be deployed independently.
serviceModeNewDescription: Register the service as a new component in the dashboard.
serviceModeExistingDescription: Use an already running DTR or submodel service.
validationInvalidBpn: Use the format BPNL followed by 12 letters or numbers.
validationInvalidConnectorName: Use only lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. The name must start and end with a letter or number.
validationInvalidResourceName: Use {min} to {max} lowercase letters, numbers or hyphens, without spaces.
validationDuplicateName: This name is already in use. Please choose a different one.
validationInvalidUrl: Enter a valid URL starting with http:// or https://.
connectorLimitReached: A maximum of {max} EDC connectors can be deployed.
connectorAddComponentTooltip: Add one or more new components for this connector.
deploymentStatusDeployingConnectorMessag: The connector deployment has started. The platform is now preparing the connector in the background.
deploymentStatusDeployingComponentMessag: The component deployment has started. The platform is now preparing the component in the background.
deploymentStatusSuccessConnectorMessage: The connector deployment was submitted successfully.
deploymentStatusSuccessComponentMessage: The component deployment was submitted successfully.
deploymentStatusErrorConnectorMessage: The connector deployment could not be submitted. Please review the configuration and try again.
deploymentStatusErrorComponentMessage: The component deployment could not be submitted. Please review the configuration and try again.
deploymentStatusDashboardHint: The deployment may need a short time before the final status is visible on the dashboard.
connectorDeleteTooltipWithoutComponents: Deletes the connector from the dashboard and uninstalls the related deployment from the cluster.
connectorDeleteIntro: Do you really want to delete "{name}"?
connectorDeleteBody: This removes the connector from the dashboard and uninstalls the related Helm deployment from the cluster.
deleteComponentFollowup: The component will be removed from the dashboard overview. If it was already connected technically, please review the related target environment or service configuration afterwards.
deleteComponentTooltip: Deletes this component from the dashboard overview after confirmation.
statsDataSpaceContent: This card shows the loaded dataspace name and often the main identifier for the environment you are working in.
statsDataSpaceFooter: If values are missing here, check Dataspace Settings or the central platform configuration.
statsHealthContent: Users can quickly see whether the console and its connected capabilities appear generally healthy.
statsHealthFooter: Use this as a first orientation point before diving into connectors or services.
statsActivityContent: This card helps users understand whether logs, synchronization or background processes are currently active.
statsActivityFooter: If something looks unusual, compare the activity state with the tables below.
statsConnectorsContent: Shows how many EDC connectors are currently known and how many appear active.
statsConnectorsFooter: A strong starting point for non-technical users: check this card first, then use Add+ if you need a new connector.
statsAddContent: After clicking, the app asks whether you want an EDC connector or a component/service, then guides you step by step through the required information.
statsAddItemConnector: EDC Connector: use when you want to deploy a new data exchange instance.
statsAddItemComponent: Component / Service: use when you want to attach a business or platform service to an existing connector.
statsAddItemValues: Values such as URLs or credentials usually come from platform docs, the DevOps team, or the service owner.
statsAddFooter: If you are unsure, start with a connector first and add components afterwards.
monitorDescription: Monitor connectors, linked services, recent activity and recommended next steps in one operational view.
statusOverallHealthSubtitle: Combines connector, service and warning state
statusHealthyConnectorsSubtitle: Connectors in healthy or active state
statusRecentEventsSubtitleBackend: Loaded directly from backend activity logs
statusRecentEventsSubtitleDerived: Derived from known connector and component data
monitorConnectorHealthDescription: Status, responsiveness and dependencies of your EDC connectors.
monitorServiceHealthDescription: Overview of DTR and submodel services and how they are linked to connectors.
eventComponentDeployedBody: {type} was deployed as an independent component.
eventConnectorAvailableHealthy: The connector is known in the dashboard and can be used for additional services.
eventConnectorAvailableUnhealthy: The last known state is critical. Check endpoint and platform reachability.
recommendationUnhealthyConnectors: {count} connector(s) report a critical state. Check endpoint and cluster reachability first.
recommendationNoConnectors: There are no connectors yet. Start with ADD and deploy your first EDC connector.
recommendationStable: Your monitored resources currently look stable. Use monitoring for regular checks and trend observation.
onboardingWelcomeTitle: Welcome to the EDC Management Console!
onboardingWelcomeSubtitle: Manage your EDC connectors and monitor your data flows in real-time.
onboardingOverviewSubtitle: Understand the main areas of your dashboard.
onboardingGettingStartedSubtitle: How to deploy your first EDC connector.
onboardingSupportSubtitle: We are here to help you.
onboardingWelcomeIntro: This guide will walk you through the main features of the console and show you how to get started.
onboardingCanDoItem1: Create, manage and monitor EDC connectors
onboardingCanDoItem2: Track system health and connector status in real-time
onboardingCanDoItem4: Export reports and share updates with your team
onboardingOverviewStatusCardsBody: Shows key metrics like data space, system health, activity status and connector count with real-time updates.
onboardingOverviewConnectorTableBody: Overview of all EDC connectors with status, version, endpoint and quick actions.
onboardingOverviewNavigationBody: Quick access to Dashboard, Monitor, App and Dataspace Settings.
onboardingStep1Body: Click the orange "Add+" button to create a new connector.
onboardingStep2Body: Follow the step-by-step wizard to configure your connector with clear descriptions for each step.
onboardingStep3Body: Track your connector status in the table and receive notifications for any issues.
onboardingTipBody: Hover over buttons and icons to see tooltips with additional information.
onboardingSupportIntro: If you have questions while using the console:
onboardingSupportInlineBody: Tooltips and contextual help are available throughout the application. Hover over elements to learn more.
onboardingSupportConfirmBody: Important actions require confirmation, so you always know what will happen before changes are made.
onboardingSupportResponsiveBody: The interface is designed for desktop, zoom levels and mobile layouts so your workflow stays stable.
onboardingReadyBody: You can reopen this guide anytime through the help button or from settings.
statsDigitalTwinRegistriesContent: Shows how many digital twin registries are deployed and how many of the {max} available slots are still free.
statsDigitalTwinRegistriesFooter: Once the limit is reached, delete an existing registry before deploying another.
statsSubmodelServicesContent: Shows how many submodel services are deployed and how many of the {max} available slots are still free.
statsSubmodelServicesFooter: Once the limit is reached, delete an existing service before deploying another.
componentTypeLimitReached: A maximum of {max} {type} instances can be deployed.
componentAllLimitsReached: Every component type has reached its deployment limit.
componentLimitBlockedHint: Delete an existing one on the dashboard to free up a slot.
